steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure to style
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a basic structure containing headings, paragraphs, and a navigation menu that we'll later style for print. Use the following structure: a header with a navigation menu, a main content area with a heading and paragraphs, and a footer.

<html>
<head>
    <title>Print Styles Lesson</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add header with navigation menu, main content with heading and paragraphs, and a footer here -->
</body>
</html>

steps.title: Add basic screen styles to the content
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules inside a <style> element in the <head> to style the HTML elements for normal screen viewing. Style the body with a light background, the header with a dark background and white text, and paragraphs with a readable font size and line height.
steps.hint: Place a <style> tag in the <head> section and write CSS rules for body, header, and p elements.

    <!-- Add <style> element with CSS for screen viewing here -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add header with navigation menu, main content with heading and paragraphs, and a footer here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file now includes a <style> element with CSS rules that style the body, header, and paragraphs for screen display.
successCriteria: A <style> element is added in the <head> with CSS rules for body, header, and p elements that define colors, font, and spacing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added basic screen styles. This sets up the visual appearance for normal viewing before we adjust for printing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styles, but make sure to include rules for body, header, and p elements with properties like background-color, color, font-size, and padding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS for screen viewing is missing or incomplete. Add a <style> element in the <head> with rules for body, header, and p elements to style them for normal display.

steps.instruction: Inside the existing <style> element, add an @media print rule that will contain all print-specific styles.
steps.hint: Use the syntax @media print { /* your print styles will go here */ }
